Quality Strategy 2022  
University of Bern

Quality assurance and development as a participatory system and a culture that permeates the entire university.

The Quality Strategy 2022 was approved on May 5, 2022 by the Commission for Quality Assurance and Development and approved on May 10, 2022 by the University Executive Board. It replaces the Quality Strategy 2018–2021 from September 11, 2018.
Vice Rectorate for Quality

Page 2/13

According to Strategy 2030, quality assurance and development is one of seven functional strategies that are of central importance for the functioning of the university. In this context, the University of Bern uses the system of quality assurance and development to continuously improve its performance. The faculties formulate their contribution to the realization of the functional strategies as well as their specific goals through faculty strategies. Central components of the quality management system are the quality strategy and action plans at the university and faculty level for their implementation.

The Quality Strategy 2022 of the University of Bern defines the framework for the measures of quality assurance and quality development (QSE) and illustrates the functioning of the quality management system. In doing so, the quality management system is sustainably developed, and values as well as the self-perception for the university's quality culture are established. The university's QSE is based on a lived quality culture, efficient governance, as well as measures and processes for implementing QSE.

The QSE at the University of Bern is designed as a participatory system, integrated into the existing management systems. The QSE is conceived as an open, dynamic system, which is continuously developed in terms of content. This allows the University of Bern, through guided self-reflection – if necessary with the involvement of external expertise – to flexibly adapt to external circumstances and developments. The quality assurance system ensures the implementation of the university strategy and the development of the University of Bern.

All areas of the University of Bern are regularly evaluated. In this way, the quality of the university’s services is continuously reviewed, and a common quality culture is developed, which at the same time respects the particularities of the different teaching and research cultures of the faculties and their autonomy. The maxim applies: "As differentiated as (academically) necessary, as uniform (and comparable) as possible."

Quality Culture
Quality culture consists of structural-formal and organizational psychological elements (Sonntag and Sattler 2017). Structural-formal elements are found at the normative, strategic, and operational levels of quality assurance. These are, in particular, regulations, directives, as well as for teaching and research, and the services of the central QSE department, guidelines and specific evaluation instruments. Central organizational psychological elements for developing a shared quality culture are leadership philosophy, participation, communication, commitment, engagement, and sense of responsibility.

The QSE at the University of Bern is strongly participatory. All university members contribute through their involvement in bodies such as commissions and committees, or steer it through their participation in the development, improvement, and review of work (feedback, exchange, etc.). Effort is made to keep processes lean, in order to reduce the burden on faculty management and to maintain a high level of participation by members of the university in the long term.

The QSE System
To formulate, achieve, and maintain the highest quality objectives, the University of Bern is guided by the quality cycle (Deming cycle, PDCA cycle), as shown in Figure 1. The relevant objectives are primarily found in Strategy 2030, in the performance mandate of the cantonal council to the University of Bern for the years 2022 – 2025, the institutional accreditation process report, as well as in the functional strategies (Appendix 1). Quality management is that part of the quality assurance system that defines and implements measures to achieve the quality objectives. The measures to implement quality objectives are recorded in the University Action Plan and in the Faculty Action Plans. Based on the Faculty Action Plans and the annual strategy discussions with the faculties and centers, it is verified whether the set objectives have been achieved. The information obtained from analyses and evaluations flows back into planning, thus closing the control loop.

3

This leads to process optimization and to measures that improve the structure. Quality control also includes quality reporting. This involves transparent documentation of efforts to improve quality and of measures and process adjustments. It thus provides evidence, for example through accreditation, that quality requirements are being met.

The University Action Plan lists all measures of the university’s QSE and is thus the most comprehensive measures document for QSE. Together, the University and the Faculty Action Plans make visible all university, faculty-specific and center-specific measures of quality assurance and development, and serve as strategic controlling of the implementation of Strategy 2030 and the faculty strategies. The Action Plans are structured along the four pillars of the university Tasks, Personnel, Cross-sectional topics, Resources, and in the category Governance.

Measures of the University Action Plan that fall under the responsibility of the faculties or centers are listed in the Faculty Action Plans. The measures from the University Action Plan provide the framework for the minimum requirements in implementation. The Faculty Action Plans specify how the measures that fall under the responsibility of the faculties are implemented in a faculty- and center-specific manner. To implement the faculty strategies, the Faculty Action Plans are updated with additional measures based on the objectives of the faculty strategies.

With the Quality Strategy 2022, the University Action Plan, and the Faculty Action Plans, the University of Bern has the necessary instruments to develop the desired unified quality culture and to set priorities in implementation. The jointly defined values and objectives promote the quality awareness of university members and shared values regarding quality. Everyone who researches, teaches, studies, and works at the University of Bern, as well as all organizational units and committees, share responsibility for the quality of the university’s services.

Figure 1: Quality management at the University of Bern; source: own depiction based on Deming 1982.

4

Holistic Approach of the University QSE System
In line with Strategy 2030, the quality standards for institutional accreditation (according to Art. 22, Paragraph 1 of the Accreditation Ordinance HFKG, Appendix 2) and the self-conception of the University of Bern, a model was developed that incorporates all university areas into the QSE. The model thus includes those areas prescribed by the accreditation guidelines, which must be covered by the quality assurance system. These areas are assigned to the four pillars of Tasks, Personnel, Cross-sectional topics or Resources, while Governance acts as the roof.

The quality assurance system of the University of Bern pursues a comprehensive approach aimed at permanently ensuring quality as a system goal. The quality assurance system takes adequate account of the particularities of a university (especially academic freedom). QSE measures include on the one hand the university’s core tasks of teaching, research, services, and continuing education as well as all university members from professors to students (Figure 2), and on the other hand the cross-sectional topics of gender equality, sustainable development, internationalization, communication, and digitalization as well as resources such as staff recruitment and development, finance, infrastructure, administration and operations, and risk management.

Figure 2: The university QSE model pursues a comprehensive approach; source: own depiction

Page 5/13

Appendix 1: Principles, Goals, and Fields of Action from Strategy 2030, the performance mandate of the cantonal government, the process report of the institutional accreditation, and functional strategies, which serve as the basis for the measures of the University Action Plan

Governance: Principles
•
The University of Bern fulfills its mission at a high level. It is committed to self-control and regularly reviews its performance and tasks. It creates the conditions to respond flexibly and in a differentiated way to the demands placed on it.
•
The University of Bern increasingly uses the quality assurance and development system (QSE) to systematically review the achievement of its goals, to support their realization, and to continuously improve its performance.
•
The University of Bern promotes the internal university discussion culture regarding quality and is guided by national and international quality standards.
•
The University Executive Board coordinates the implementation of the sub-strategies1 as well as the functional strategies2 within the framework of Strategy 2030.
•
For the implementation of Strategy 2030, management tools with different time horizons are used in planning and review.
•
The University of Bern consistently integrates the planning and review of the implementation of the quality strategy into its management cycle, at all organizational levels.
•
The University of Bern makes decisions on the basis of reliable information. For this purpose, it collects quantitative and qualitative data that are important for the management of the University of Bern.
•
The University of Bern promotes the participation of all its members. It involves them in self-administration and includes them in decision-making processes.

Governance: Goals and Fields of Action
•
Central components of the system are the quality strategy and action plans at university and faculty levels for their implementation. The use of these instruments is continually optimized.
•
In balancing disciplinary/faculty interests and university-wide interests, the maxim should be followed: “As differentiated as (academically) necessary, as uniform (and comparable) as possible.”
•
The effectiveness and efficiency of feedback loops are critically reviewed and strengthened at all organizational levels.
•
Following the communications concept for university QSE, the internal university discussion culture on quality is promoted. All university members are thus comprehensively and adequately informed about measures, processes and results of the university QSE and involved in its development.
•
Establish the adapted management cycle for planning and reviewing the implementation of Strategy 2030.
•
Review the governance structure with regard to “checks and balances” and strategic inputs from the national and international environment.
•
Review the framework conditions for structured participation of administrative and technical staff.

Teaching: Principles
•
The University of Bern sharpens its profile as an educational institution with excellent teaching. It remains a campus university, but makes teaching more interactive and expands it with new teaching and learning formats and targeted use of new digital solutions.
•
The University of Bern promotes effective teaching and self-directed study.
•
The University of Bern promotes innovative teaching.
•
The University of Bern leverages its potential as a full university and enhances inter- and transdisciplinarity. The added value created by the broad subject range of the faculties should be actively promoted and made visible.
•
The University strengthens Bern as a center of medicine.
•
The University promotes digital transformation in teaching at the University of Bern.
•
The University plays an active role in the digital transformation of education and participates in the exchange between different educational institutions.
•
In teaching, instruments for evaluating courses or study programs and degree programs are used.
•
Acquisition of intercultural competence and language skills complements study at the University of Bern. The offering and use of different languages in teaching, research, administration, and advising are systematized within the framework of a language policy.
•
The quality of study programs continues to increase.

Teaching: Goals and Fields of Action
•
Inter- and transdisciplinarity in teaching should be strengthened by greater permeability of structures at the levels of faculties, departments, and institutes. To this end, faculties and university management develop strategic centers, graduate schools, competence centers, platforms, and networks. In these, inter- and/or transdisciplinary teaching is carried out with a view to common strategic objectives.
•
The University of Bern sets itself apart nationally and internationally with excellent teaching, especially in selected thematic focus areas in which it has particular strengths and which are of great social and scientific importance: Sustainability, Health and Medicine, Matter and Universe, Intercultural Knowledge, Politics and Administration.

1 Full university, Five thematic focus areas, Excellent teaching, Promotion of early-career researchers, Digital transformation, Further development of infrastructure
2 Communication, Personnel development, Equality and equal opportunities, Quality assurance and development, Sustainable development, Internationalization, Lifelong learning

6

•
The University of Bern optimizes face-to-face teaching, makes teaching more interactive, expands it with new teaching and learning formats, with targeted use of new digital solutions and inclusion of new insights from teaching and learning research.
•
The University strengthens Bern as a center of medicine by establishing the School of Medical & Precision Engineering (together with the BFH), as well as through the impact of centers such as sitem-insel AG and the Bern Center for Precision Medicine (BCPM), and establishing the Multidisciplinary Center for Infectious Diseases (MCID).
•
The topic of sustainable development is included in all study programs and degree programs at the University of Bern.
•
The University participates in shaping the BeLEARN Center for the digital transformation in education.
•
Findings from research into the opportunities and risks of digitalization, security and data protection aspects, and responsible implementation of digitalization are incorporated into teaching.
•
The University of Bern offers at least one bachelor's or master's degree program in each subject area: Theology, Linguistics and Literary Studies, Historical and Cultural Sciences, Social Sciences, Economics, Law, Exact and Natural Sciences, Veterinary Medicine and Medicine, as well as in the interdisciplinary subject area.
•
When designing teaching, particular attention is paid to the coherence and consistency of the study program, transitions between study levels, and the bridges from school to university and from university to the workplace.
•
Teaching and examination methods are aligned with learning objectives (learning outcomes).
•
Quality assurance in teaching is consolidated. This includes the systematic evaluation of courses and study programs and degrees, and where sensible, accreditation (bachelor's and master's programs in Medicine, Pharmacy, and Veterinary Medicine) as well as consistent implementation of the results from evaluations. The QSE guidelines for the university's core areas of teaching, research, continuing education, and services contain appropriate and binding processes for evaluations of courses, assessments, and study programs and degrees.
•
QSE in teaching is a criterion and subject in the performance agreements with the faculties and the performance mandates to the competence centers.
•
High-quality infrastructure and easy access to modern work media are ensured.

Research: Principles
•
The University of Bern leverages its potential as a full university and enhances inter- and transdisciplinarity. The added value created by the broad subject range of the faculties should be actively promoted and made visible.
•
The University of Bern stands for freedom of research and teaching and is independent.
•
The profiling in the following five thematic focus areas, in which the University of Bern has particular strengths and which are of great social and scientific importance, is sought: Sustainability, Health and Medicine, Matter and Universe, Intercultural Knowledge, Politics and Administration.
•
On the basis of being a full university, the University of Bern develops inter- and/or transdisciplinary competence centers that meet the highest scientific standards.
•
The University of Bern aligns itself in teaching, research, and services with the highest scientific and ethical quality standards.
•
The University of Bern positions itself as a capital city university with close ties to application partners in politics and administration and strengthens Bern as a center of medicine.
•
The University of Bern makes its scientific insights and findings accessible to the scientific community and all interested parties.
•
The University of Bern fosters knowledge and technology transfer.
•
The University of Bern evaluates research performance and provides units with key performance indicators.
•
At greater intervals, the research output of units is evaluated by external peers within the framework of clear questions. This is done with the aim of establishing position, sharpening profile, and developing possibilities for advancement.

Research: Goals and Fields of Action
•
Competitive third-party funding is acquired while safeguarding the freedom of teaching and research.
•
The University of Bern enables thematic shifts in subject areas and further develops thematic priorities.
•
Inter- and transdisciplinarity is implemented across faculty boundaries.
•
As a capital city university and internationally recognized center of medicine, it is oriented towards stakeholders in the catchment area, harnesses synergies, and ensures transfer and translation in cooperation with other research institutions, politics, and business.
•
The quantitative key figures from research evaluations are supplemented by qualitative indicators, which are mainly used in peer reviews and ensure a certain standardization. Here, as with quantitative measures, care is taken that they meet the needs of the subject area, but also the requirements of the University of Bern.

Services3: Principles
•
Services should not become a primary goal and must be closely connected to university teaching and research.
•
The University of Bern offers services to the public for which it is especially qualified due to its scientific work and methodological expertise.

3 The following organizational units provide permanent services according to university regulations Art. 110: Institut für Infektionskrankheiten, Institut für Pathologie, Institut für Rechtsmedizin, Zahnmedizinische Kliniken, Departement für klinische Veterinärmedizin, Institut für Parasitologie, Institut für Tierpathologie, Institut für Veterinär-Bakteriologie, Zentrum für Fisch- und Wildtiermedizin. They belong either to the Faculty of Medicine or to the Vetsuisse Faculty (not all units of these faculties are service units).

7

Services: Goals and Fields of Action
•
Units with a service mission run active quality management and are certified or accredited wherever possible and sensible.
•
Services must be paid for by recipients; compensation should be cost-covering.

Continuing Education: Principles
•
The University of Bern offers a varied and high-quality range of postgraduate study programs and courses with regional, national, and international appeal.
•
The programs are based on the “Key values of higher education continuing education” of Swissuniversities, the recommendations for quality development in university continuing education from Swissuni (in collaboration with the Accreditation and Quality Assurance Agency of Swiss Universities), and subject-specifically on relevant international standards.

Continuing Education: Goals and Fields of Action
•
Planning of postgraduate programs is preceded by a careful needs, supply, and market analysis.
•
Postgraduate programs combine academic rigor with practice and transfer orientation. They are based on the current state of research and established best practices.
•
Target groups and learning objectives are defined.
•
Postgraduate programs comply in scope and title with the requirements of the University of Bern.
•
Admission requirements are clearly defined and guarantee equality before the law. They are published and adhered to.
•
The programs are based on a study regulation and a study plan.
•
Decision-making paths, competences, and responsibilities are defined and communicated to all involved persons. Administrative processes are efficient and customer-oriented.
•
The programs are economically viable and have adequate financial, infrastructural, and didactic resources to achieve their objectives.
•
Instructors are academic specialists or experts from practice. They possess the necessary specialist knowledge. They are pedagogically and didactically competent.
•
Didactic means correspond to the current standard and are tailored to the different competence profiles and professional situations of the students.
•
The programs pursue a multifaceted and impact-oriented approach to quality development that takes account of the particularities of university continuing education. The persons responsible for the programs take appropriate measures to promote and monitor quality development. The decision-making processes, competences, and responsibilities in quality development are defined and communicated to all involved persons.

Professors: Principles
•
In their role as supervisors, professors consider the leadership of staff to be a core responsibility. They constantly develop their leadership skills.
•
The qualifications and competences of professors are of particular importance for the quality of the University of Bern’s output. This is reflected in a structural and appointment process which meets the usual standards of quality assurance.
•
The University of Bern promotes exchange between academia and industry, particularly at the professorial level.
•
At the professorial level, the University of Bern pays attention to making career paths for early-career researchers attractive. This particularly concerns the models SNF-Eccellenza Professorial / PRIMA Fellowships4 as well as Assistant Professorships with and without Tenure Track.

Professors: Goals and Fields of Action
•
The University of Bern supports professors in further developing their leadership skills through appropriate opportunities.
•
The structural reporting process is standardized and strengthened as a management tool via the targeted integration of feedback loops.
•
Professorships are preferably advertised as Assistant Professorships with Tenure Track (APTT). For strategic and structural reasons, such a position can also be advertised “open rank”. The new structural reporting process will be used university-wide after a testing and adaptation phase.
•
SNF-Eccellenza Professorial / PRIMA Fellowships and Assistant Professorships are part of the professorial faculty, thereby strengthening their independence and scope for development at the University of Bern.
•
The treatment of SNF-Eccellenza Professorial / PRIMA Fellowships and Assistant Professorships at the University of Bern is standardized.
•
The APTT is an attractive model for advanced postdocs as a pathway to a permanent professorship. APTT offers the opportunity for long-term career planning and functions as an instrument of the University of Bern to retain excellent scientists at a stage of high creativity and productivity.
Lecturers: Principles
•
The lectureship is an attractive alternative career goal to the professorship.

4 In the future, this funding category will be split into two pots: "Eccellenza Professorial Fellowships" (the previous SNF funding professorships) and "Eccellenza Grants" (competitive funding for APTT in the first 18 months of their appointment).

8

Lecturers: Goals and Fields of Action
•
Lectureships have complete academic independence, which is a prerequisite for independently acquiring third-party funding.
•
Lectureships are filled through transparent recruitment procedures and with a faculty appointment committee.
•
Additionally, an associate professorship may be awarded.
•
With the new Assistant Lectureship with Tenure Track (ADTT), a career path with a probationary period has been created (analogous to APTT) with a view to permanent employment.

Early Career Researchers: Principles
•
The University of Bern stands out for its targeted promotion of early-career researchers and supports the entire spectrum of development from the doctoral level with appropriate resources.
•
The University of Bern creates appropriate employment conditions for researchers, trains them to become internationally competitive early-career researchers, develops support concepts for junior researchers, and is committed to equality and the compatibility of work and family life.
•
The University of Bern regards good conditions for academic early-career researchers as an important prerequisite for good teaching, research, continuing education, and services.
•
The University of Bern operates a Competence Center for the academic careers of mid-level staff (advice, mentoring, grants, training offers, information, etc.).
•
The University of Bern improves conditions and qualification opportunities for early-career researchers.

Early Career Researchers: Goals and Fields of Action
•
The University of Bern follows an academic career model, which ideally looks as follows:
  o The doctorate is usually completed in 4 years; doctoral candidates have sufficient personal research time regardless of funding source. Each doctorate is based on a binding agreement, and at a minimum, the principle of dual supervision applies.
  o In addition to the classic individual doctorate, the University of Bern offers structured research-accompanying doctoral programs (e.g. Graduate Schools).
  o In the early postdoc phase (i.e. up to a maximum of 3 years after the doctorate), the decision about an academic career must be made. In the advanced postdoc phase (from approx. 3 years after the doctorate), the independent position must be built. Postdocs have a protected research time of at least 50% and are entitled to coaching and support, e.g., in career development discussions. Each postdoc is based on an agreement.
  o The lectureship is an attractive, alternative career goal to the professorship. It has different (but not exclusive) emphases in research and teaching. With the ADTT, an independent career path with a probationary period towards a position as a lecturer has been created (analogous to APTT).
  o The APTT is an attractive model for advanced postdocs as a path towards a permanent position as professor.
•
To implement this career model, the University of Bern, in collaboration with the faculties and the mid-level staff, has developed a catalog of measures tailored for each faculty, taking subject-specific characteristics into account. The goals have been linked with faculty performance agreements; they are reviewed and further developed in the context of annual strategy discussions as well as through regular evaluation.
•
The mid-level staff is supported and promoted in securing third-party funding.

Students: Principles
•
The University of Bern is attractive to students, especially those from Bern.
•
The university safeguards the interests of francophone students.
•
The University of Bern enables its graduates to use digital transformation productively for their own activities and to help shape it innovatively.
•
Early involvement of students in research and teaching is actively encouraged.
•
The University of Bern offers its students an international campus.
•
With innovative formats, the international exchange of students is made sustainable.
•
The university prepares students optimally for the future.

Students: Goals and Fields of Action
•
The University of Bern offers a point of contact "Chargé-e des affaires francophones" for francophone students.
•
A steady influx of students from the canton of Bern and a stable number of students from other cantons and from abroad should be secured.
•
The University of Bern has sufficient and appropriate resources and infrastructure to support the learning process of students.
•
Civic engagement by students is encouraged by providing appropriate incentives.

Administrative Staff: Principles
•
The University of Bern fosters cooperation and mutual understanding among academia, teaching, and administration to deliver high-quality and efficient overall performance.

9

•
The University of Bern aligns personnel management with a personnel strategy for all staff of the university.

Administrative Staff: Goals and Fields of Action
•
The University of Bern encourages exchange between academia, teaching, and administration. Processes and procedures in administration are communicated transparently.
•
A personnel strategy for all staff of the university, in addition to the existing strategy for promoting early-career researchers, will be developed.

•

Title: Qualität Team
text:
Die Abteilung für Qualitätssicherung und -entwicklung (Abteilung QSE) unterstützt die Universitätsangehörigen in der Qualitätssicherung und Qualitätsentwicklung (QSE), fördert die universitäre Qualitätskultur und hilft bei der Entwicklung und Umsetzung von QSE-Massnahmen.

In Zusammenarbeit mit den Vizerektoraten, dem Stab der Universitätsleitung und allen universitären Einheiten stellt die Abteilung QSE die Koordination und Umsetzung der Qualitätsstrategie in allen universitären Bereichen sicher (Evaluationen von Lehrveranstaltungen https://www.unibe.ch/studium/werkzeuge_und_arbeitshilfen/fuer_lehrende/lehrveranstaltungsevaluation/index_ger.html  und Studienprogrammen https://www.unibe.ch/universitaet/portraet/selbstverstaendnis/qualitaet/kernaufgaben/lehre/index_ger.html#pane708997, Forschungsevaluationen, Evaluationen der Zentren, etc.).

Des Weiteren ist sie verantwortlich für den Prozess der institutionellen Akkreditierung der Universität, die Geschäftsführung der QSE-Kommission sowie die Vernetzung von Akteurinnen und Akteuren in qualitätsrelevanten Angelegenheiten.

Title: Gremien
text:
Kommission für Qualitätssicherung und Qualitätsentwicklung (QSE-Kommission)
Die Qualitätssicherung und -entwicklung (QSE) ist partizipativ angelegt und wird von allen Universitätsangehörigen getragen, durch die Mitarbeit in Gremien oder die direkte Beteiligung an der Entwicklung, Verbesserung und Überprüfung der Leistungen (Feedback, Austausch usw.).
Den Rahmen der gesamten QSE-Organisation bildet die Kommission für Qualitätssicherung und Qualitätsentwicklung (QSE-Kommission), die die Universitätsleitung in allen Angelegenheiten der Qualitätssicherung und Qualitätsentwicklung berät. Die Fakultäten, der Zentralbereich, der Mittelbau und die Studierenden verfügen je über eine/n Q-Beauftragte/n, der/ die Mitglied der gesamtuniversitären QSE-Kommission ist. In den Fakultäten werden die Q-Beauftragten durch Wissenschaftliche Mitarbeitende Q bzw. Q-Assistenzen und/ oder Q-Verantwortliche in ihrer Arbeit unterstützt. Die Q-Beauftragten leiten, sofern vorhanden, fakultäre QSE-Gremien, in denen die Q-Verantwortlichen die Verbindung in die Departemente und Institute der Fakultäten bilden und dort QSE-Aktivitäten fördern.
QSE-Kommission Mitglieder (https://www.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/content/e809/e810/e812/e708931/e715528/e915240/QSEMitglieder_Mai_2025_Homepage_ger.pdf)    
QSE-Kommission Geschäftsordnung (https://www.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/content/e809/e810/e812/e708931/e715528/e915243/GeschaeftsordnungQSE-K2022unterschrieben_ger.pdf)
Arbeitskreis Akkreditierung (AKKRED)
Der Arbeitskreis Akkreditierung (AKKRED), der unabhängig von der QSE-Kommission arbeitet, ist ein von der Universitätsleitung eingesetzter und aus Mitarbeitenden des Zentralbereichs gebildeter Arbeitskreis. Zu den Hauptaufgaben der Mitglieder des AKKRED zählen:
Der AKKRED unterstützt die Universitätsleitung, den Zentralbereich, die Fakultäten und die strategischen Zentren bei der Planung und Überprüfung der Umsetzung der universitären Strategie.
Überprüfung und Aktualisierung des Aktionsplans Universität gemäss Vorgaben der Universitätsleitung in Zusammenarbeit mit den zuständigen Einheiten     
Unterstützung der Fakultäten bei der jährlichen Aktualisierung der Aktionspläne Fakultäten mit Massnahmen, die der rollenden Planung zur Umsetzung der Fakultätsstrategien und der Unterstrategien im Kompetenzbereich der Universitätsleitung sowie der Integration von Massnahmen aus den Protokollen der Gespräche zu den Aktionsplänen und der Strategiegespräche dienen.
Unterstützung der strategischen Zentren bei der jährlichen Aktualisierung des Aktionsplans strategische Zentren mit Massnahmen, die der rollenden Planung zur Umsetzung der Leistungsaufträge und der Unterstrategien im Kompetenzbereich der Universitätsleitung sowie der Integration von Massnahmen aus den Protokollen der Strategiegespräche dienen.
Unterjähriger Austausch mit allen Beteiligten zum Umsetzungsstand der Massnahmen im Aktionsplan Universität, der Massnahmen in den Aktionsplänen Fakultäten und der Massnahmen im Aktionsplan strategische Zentren
AKKRED Mitglieder (https://www.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/content/e809/e810/e812/e708931/e715528/e915246/MitgliederdesArbeitskreisAkkreditierungAKKRED_20250708_ger.pdf)
AKKRED Geschäftsordnung (https://www.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/content/e809/e810/e812/e708931/e715528/e1364168/GeschaeftsordnungAKKRED_240604_ger.pdf)

Commission for Quality Assurance and Quality Development (QSE Commission)  
Quality assurance and development (QSE) is designed to be participatory and is supported by all members of the university, through participation in committees or direct involvement in the development, improvement, and review of performance (feedback, exchange, etc.).

The framework for the entire QSE organization is formed by the Commission for Quality Assurance and Quality Development (QSE Commission), which advises the university management in all matters of quality assurance and development. Each faculty, the central administration, the mid-level academic staff, and the students have a Q representative who is a member of the university-wide QSE Commission. In the faculties, the Q representatives are supported in their work by Academic Staff Q, Q assistants, and/or Q coordinators. The Q representatives, if such exist, lead faculty QSE committees, in which the Q coordinators serve as links to the departments and institutes of the faculties and promote QSE activities there.

QSE Commission Members (https://www.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/content/e809/e810/e812/e708931/e715528/e915240/QSEMitglieder_Mai_2025_Homepage_ger.pdf)  
QSE Commission Rules of Procedure (https://www.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/content/e809/e810/e812/e708931/e715528/e915243/GeschaeftsordnungQSE-K2022unterschrieben_ger.pdf)

Accreditation Working Group (AKKRED)  
The Accreditation Working Group (AKKRED), which operates independently of the QSE Commission, is a working group established by the university management and made up of staff from the central administration. The main tasks of the AKKRED members include:

- AKKRED supports the university management, the central administration, the faculties, and the strategic centers in planning and reviewing the implementation of the university strategy.
- Reviewing and updating the University Action Plan according to the requirements of the university management in cooperation with the relevant units.
- Supporting the faculties in the annual update of the Faculty Action Plans with measures that serve the rolling planning for the implementation of the faculty strategies and sub-strategies within the area of responsibility of the university management as well as integrating measures from the reports of the meetings on the action plans and strategy discussions.
- Supporting the strategic centers in the annual update of the Strategic Centers Action Plan with measures that serve the rolling planning for the implementation of the performance mandates and sub-strategies within the area of responsibility of the university management as well as integrating measures from the reports of the strategy discussions.
- Ongoing exchange with all stakeholders regarding the status of the implementation of the measures in the University Action Plan, the measures in the Faculty Action Plans, and the measures in the Strategic Centers Action Plan.

AKKRED Members (https://www.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/content/e809/e810/e812/e708931/e715528/e915246/MitgliederdesArbeitskreisAkkreditierungAKKRED_20250708_ger.pdf)  
AKKRED Rules of Procedure (https://www.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/content/e809/e810/e812/e708931/e715528/e1364168/GeschaeftsordnungAKKRED_240604_ger.pdf)

Title: Anerkennung hervorragender Leistungen in der Lehre (ALL)
text:
Anerkennung hervorragender Leistungen in der Lehre (ALL) Kontakt

Fachstelle Lehrveranstaltungs-evaluation
Vizerektorat Qualität und Nachhaltige Entwicklung
Hochschulstrasse 6
3012 Bern
Schweiz
Kontaktperson
Magdalena Dampz
E-Mail-Adresse
magdalena.dampz@unibe.ch

Mit der Auszeichnung anerkennt und würdigt die Universität das Engagement ihrer Dozierenden für hervorragende Lehre.

ALL trägt dazu bei, die Lehrqualität zu steigern, die Wertschätzung für exzellente Lehre zu fördern und die Entwicklung der guten Lehre an der Universität Bern insgesamt voranzutreiben. Ausserdem wird besonders dem Mittelbau dadurch die Möglichkeit gegeben, sich auch in der Lehre zu profilieren.

Die Kriterien, der Ablauf des Auswahlprozesses sowie die Form der Auszeichnung sind im "Konzept für die Anerkennung hervorragender Leistungen in der Lehre" formuliert (intern zugänglich).

Zielsetzung

In der heutigen Zeit, in der Bildung und Wissen von entscheidender Bedeutung sind, spielen Dozierende eine zentrale Rolle. Sie vermitteln nicht nur Wissen, sondern sind auch Mentorinnen und Mentoren, die Studierende inspirieren, ermutigen und unterstützen. Herausragende Lehrveranstaltungen können das Leben und die berufliche Laufbahn der Studierenden nachhaltig prägen. Angesichts dieser Bedeutung würdigt die Universität Bern hervorragend evaluierte Lehrveranstaltungen und stellt sie beispielhaft ins Schaufenster. 
Zudem wird besonders dem Mittelbau dadurch die Möglichkeit gegeben, sich auch in der Lehre zu profilieren und bei Bewerbungen eine offizielle Bestätigung positiv evaluierter Lehrveranstaltungen vorweisen zu können.

Ablauf
Die Fakultäten bzw. Institute bestimmen, welche Lehrveranstaltungen im jeweiligen Semester evaluiert werden (s. Rahmenkonzept). (Vorerst werden die Evaluationen der Medizinischen Fakultät nicht berücksichtigt, da diese eine andere Evaluationsform verwendet.)
Die Fachstelle Lehrveranstaltungsevaluation (Abt. QSE, Vizerektorat Qualität und Nachhaltige Entwicklung) evaluiert die ausgewählten Lehrveranstaltungen.
Nach der Durchführung und Auswertung aller Evaluationen nominiert die Fachstelle Lehrveranstaltungsevaluation für das HS jeweils ca. Mitte März und für das FS jeweils ca. Mitte September diejenigen Dozierenden, deren Lehrveranstaltung die festgelegten Kriterien erfüllen.
Die Fakultäten überprüfen die Nominierungen und teilen der Fachstelle Lehrveranstaltungsevaluation die ausgezeichneten Lehrveranstaltungen / Dozierenden mit. 
Die Fakultäten gelangen über den Uni internen Bereich zu der Anerkennungsvorlage, ergänzen sie mit den entsprechenden Angaben und drucken das Diplom aus. Das Diplom wird von der Dekanin bzw. dem Dekan unterschrieben und den betreffenden Personen übergeben.
Die Fachstelle Lehrveranstaltungsevaluation publiziert die ausgezeichneten Lehrveranstaltungen / Dozierenden auf der Website.

Kriterien
Um für ALL nominiert zu werden, muss eine Lehrveranstaltung in der Schlussevaluation ein «hervorragendes» Gesamtergebnis erreichen. Ausschlaggebend für die Einstufung in die Erfolgsstufe «hervorragend» sind dabei die Ergebnisse in den Kategorien «Lernfortschritt» und «Zufriedenheit». 

Seit HS22 gilt für die Stufe «hervorragend» der Schwellenwert ≥ 5.7. Mehr Informationen dazu erhalten Sie hier

Zusätzlich zu diesem universitätsweiten Kriterium können Fakultäten individuelle Kriterien für die Vergabe von ALL definieren:

Zusätzliche ALL Kriterien Fakultäten
 
Fakultät Phil-Hist hat folgende Zusätzliche Kriterien seit HS22. Zusätzlich zur Gesamtnote von mind. 5.7 müssen die Veranstaltungen folgende Mindestnoten für die beiden Indikatoren Lernfortschritt und Zufriedenheit aufweisen:
Veranstaltungen mit 1 – 10 Umfrageteilnahmen: mind. 5.65
Veranstaltungen mit 11 – 20 Umfrageteilnahmen: mind. 5.55 
Veranstaltungen mit 21 – 30 Umfrageteilnahmen: mind. 5.45
Veranstaltungen ab 31 Umfrageteilnahmen: mind. 5.35
Bei Veranstaltungen mit weniger als 15 Evaluationsbögen wird beim Institut nachgefragt, ob die Veranstaltung nicht deutlich mehr Teilnehmende hatte. Bei 6 oder weniger Evaluationsbögen wird beim Institut nachgefragt, ob die Auszeichnung in Ordnung geht. Veranstaltungen mit geringerer Beteiligung des/der Dozierenden (z.B. Forschungskolloquien, Ringvorlesungen) sind von ALL ausgeschlossen.

Fakultät Phil-Hum	 hat keine folgende Zusätzliche Kriterien seit HS22
 
Fakultät Phil-Nat	 hat folgende Zusätzliche Kriterien seit HS22. Es gelten Zusatzregelungen (https://www.philnat.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/fak_naturwis/content/e17097/e95924/e258233/e1702458/2025_05_Anhang4_ZusatzregelungenALL_final_ger.pdf) bezüglich Vorgehen bei Sonderfällen.

Fakultät RW	hat keine folgende Zusätzliche Kriterien seit HS22

Fakultät Theologie	 hat folgende Zusätzliche Kriterien seit HS22. Von allen als hervorragend evaluierten Lehrveranstaltungen werden die besten 5 ausgezeichnet.
Ausgeschlossen sind Exkursionen, Sozietäten und Ringvorlesungen sowie Lehrveranstaltungen mit weniger als 3 Teilnehmenden.
Für LVs mit 3 bis 6 Teilnehmenden wird ALL nur vergeben, sofern die Mehrheit der Teilnehmenden an der Evaluation teilgenommen hat.

Fakultät Vetsuisse	hat keine folgende Zusätzliche Kriterien seit HS22
 
Fakultät WiSo	hat keine folgende Zusätzliche Kriterien seit HS22
Vorerst werden die Evaluationen der Medizinischen Fakultät nicht berücksichtigt, da diese eine andere Evaluationsform verwendet.

Recognition of Outstanding Achievements in Teaching (ALL) Contact

Teaching Evaluation Unit  
Vice Rectorate for Quality and Sustainable Development  
Hochschulstrasse 6  
3012 Bern  
Switzerland  
Contact person  
Magdalena Dampz  
Email address  
magdalena.dampz@unibe.ch

With this award, the University acknowledges and honors the commitment of its instructors to outstanding teaching.

ALL contributes to improving the quality of teaching, promoting appreciation for excellent teaching, and advancing the development of good teaching at the University of Bern as a whole. In addition, it especially gives mid-level faculty the opportunity to distinguish themselves in teaching.

The criteria, the selection process, and the form of the award are set out in the “Concept for the Recognition of Outstanding Achievements in Teaching” (accessible internally).

Objective

In today’s world, where education and knowledge are of decisive importance, instructors play a central role. They do not only impart knowledge, but also serve as mentors who inspire, encourage, and support students. Outstanding courses can have a lasting impact on the lives and careers of students. In light of this significance, the University of Bern honors excellently evaluated courses and showcases them as exemplary.
Moreover, this especially gives mid-level faculty the opportunity to distinguish themselves in teaching and to present an official confirmation of positively evaluated courses in their applications.

Process
The faculties or institutes determine which courses are to be evaluated in the respective semester (see framework concept). (For the time being, evaluations from the Faculty of Medicine are not considered because a different form of evaluation is used.)
The Teaching Evaluation Unit (Dept. QSE, Vice Rectorate for Quality and Sustainable Development) evaluates the selected courses.
After the completion and analysis of all evaluations, the Teaching Evaluation Unit nominates—around mid-March for HS and around mid-September for FS—the instructors whose courses meet the established criteria.
The faculties review the nominations and inform the Teaching Evaluation Unit of the courses/instructors to be awarded.
The faculties access the recognition template via the university’s internal area, complement it with the relevant information, and print out the diploma. The diploma is signed by the dean and handed over to the respective persons.
The Teaching Evaluation Unit publishes the awarded courses/instructors on the website.

Criteria
To be nominated for ALL, a course must achieve an "outstanding" overall result in the final evaluation. Decisive for classification at the "outstanding" level are the results in the categories “learning progress” and “satisfaction.”

Since HS22, the threshold for the "outstanding" level has been ≥ 5.7. More information is available here

In addition to this university-wide criterion, faculties can define individual criteria for the awarding of ALL:

Additional ALL Criteria by Faculties

Phil-Hist Faculty has had the following additional criteria since HS22. In addition to an overall grade of at least 5.7, courses must achieve the following minimum grades for the two indicators learning progress and satisfaction:
Courses with 1–10 survey responses: at least 5.65  
Courses with 11–20 survey responses: at least 5.55  
Courses with 21–30 survey responses: at least 5.45  
Courses with 31 or more survey responses: at least 5.35  
If there are fewer than 15 evaluation forms for a course, the institute is asked whether there were not significantly more participants. If there are 6 or fewer evaluation forms, the institute is asked whether the award is acceptable. Courses with lower involvement of the instructor(s) (e.g., research colloquia, lecture series) are excluded from ALL.

Phil-Hum Faculty has had no additional criteria since HS22.

Phil-Nat Faculty has had the following additional criteria since HS22. Supplementary regulations (https://www.philnat.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/fak_naturwis/content/e17097/e95924/e258233/e1702458/2025_05_Anhang4_ZusatzregelungenALL_final_ger.pdf) apply to special cases.

RW Faculty has had no additional criteria since HS22.

Theology Faculty has had the following additional criteria since HS22. Of all courses evaluated as outstanding, the best 5 are awarded.
Excluded are excursions, societies, and lecture series, as well as courses with fewer than 3 participants.
For courses with 3 to 6 participants, ALL is only awarded if the majority of participants took part in the evaluation.

Vetsuisse Faculty has had no additional criteria since HS22.

WiSo Faculty has had no additional criteria since HS22.
For the time being, evaluations from the Faculty of Medicine are not considered because a different form of evaluation is used.

Vizerektorat Qualität und Nachhaltige Entwicklung

Kontakt
Vizerektorat Qualität und Nachhaltige Entwicklung
Universität Bern
Hochschulstrasse 6
3012 Bern
Schweiz
Sekretariat
E-Mail-Adresse
info.qualitaet@unibe.ch
Das Vizerektorat Qualität und Nachhaltige Entwicklung unterstützt die Angehörigen der Universität bei

der Förderung der Chancengleichheit
der Verankerung der Nachhaltigen Entwicklung
der Qualitätssicherung und Qualitätsentwicklung

Dienstleistungen

Chancengleichheit
Die Abteilung für Chancengleichheit berät und unterstützt die Verantwortlichen sowie alle Universitätsangehörigen. Sie bietet zudem für Mitarbeitende und Studierende verschiedene Dienstleistungen an.

Zur Chancengleichheit (https://www.unibe.ch/universitaet/organisation/leitung_und_zentralbereich/vizerektorat_qualitaet_und_nachhaltige_entwicklung/abteilung_fuer_chancengleichheit/index_ger.html)

Nachhaltige Entwicklung
Die Abteilung für Nachhaltige Entwicklung unterstützt die Integration des Querschnittsthemas Nachhaltigkeit in alle universitären Bereiche (Lehre, Forschung, Weiterbildung, Öffentlichkeitsarbeit und Betrieb), indem sie Nachhaltigkeitsaktivitäten in diesen Bereichen anregt, begleitet und vernetzt.

Zur Nachhaltigkeit (https://www.unibe.ch/universitaet/organisation/leitung_und_zentralbereich/vizerektorat_qualitaet_und_nachhaltige_entwicklung/abteilung_fuer_nachhaltige_entwicklung/index_ger.html)

Qualitätssicherung und -entwicklung
Die Abteilung für Qualitätssicherung und -entwicklung (Abteilung QSE) unterstützt die Universitätsangehörigen in der Qualitätssicherung und Qualitätsentwicklung (QSE) (https://www.unibe.ch/universitaet/portraet/selbstverstaendnis/qualitaet/index_ger.html), fördert die Qualitätskultur und hilft bei der Entwicklung und Umsetzung von QSE-Massnahmen.

Zur Abteilung QSE (https://www.unibe.ch/universitaet/organisation/leitung_und_zentralbereich/vizerektorat_qualitaet_und_nachhaltige_entwicklung/abteilung_qse/index_ger.html)

Projekt Kompass UniBE - Hochschulvorbereitung für geflüchtete Studierende
Das Projektteam Kompass UniBE berät und unterstützt studieninteressierte Geflüchtete bei einer Zulassung zu einem Studium an der Universität Bern. Mit dem Projekt Kompass UniBE bietet sie ein Hochschulvorbereitungsjahr an.

Zur Hochschulvorbereitung (https://www.unibe.ch/universitaet/organisation/leitung_und_zentralbereich/vizerektorat_qualitaet_und_nachhaltige_entwicklung/kompass_unibe/index_ger.html)

Förderung einer aktiven Engagementkultur an der UniBE und darüber hinaus
Engaged UniBE ist eine Initiative der Universität Bern, die die Verankerung der Universität in der Gesellschaft zum Ziel hat. Sie gestaltet mit Stakeholdern aus Bern, der Region und dem Kanton Bern sowie darüber hinaus gesellschaftliche Entwicklungen.
Mit Engaged UniBE wird der Wissenstransfer gefördert, in dem Studierende, Lehrende und Mitarbeitende in ihrem Engagement und Austausch mit der Gesellschaft unterstützt werden.

Mehr zu Engaged UniBE (https://engaged.unibe.ch/index_ger.html)

The Vice-Rectorate for Quality and Sustainable Development supports the members of the university in

- the promotion of equal opportunities
- the anchoring of sustainable development
- quality assurance and quality development

Services

Equal Opportunities  
The Equal Opportunities Department advises and supports those responsible as well as all members of the university. In addition, it offers various services for employees and students.

About Equal Opportunities (https://www.unibe.ch/universitaet/organisation/leitung_und_zentralbereich/vizerektorat_qualitaet_und_nachhaltige_entwicklung/abteilung_fuer_chancengleichheit/index_ger.html)

Sustainable Development  
The Department for Sustainable Development supports the integration of the cross-cutting topic of sustainability into all university areas (teaching, research, continuing education, public relations, and operations) by stimulating, accompanying, and networking sustainability activities in these areas.

About Sustainability (https://www.unibe.ch/universitaet/organisation/leitung_und_zentralbereich/vizerektorat_qualitaet_und_nachhaltige_entwicklung/abteilung_fuer_nachhaltige_entwicklung/index_ger.html)

Quality Assurance and Development  
The Department for Quality Assurance and Development (Department QSE) supports university members in quality assurance and quality development (QSE) (https://www.unibe.ch/universitaet/portraet/selbstverstaendnis/qualitaet/index_ger.html), promotes the quality culture, and assists with the development and implementation of QSE measures.

About the QSE Department (https://www.unibe.ch/universitaet/organisation/leitung_und_zentralbereich/vizerektorat_qualitaet_und_nachhaltige_entwicklung/abteilung_qse/index_ger.html)

Project Kompass UniBE – University Preparation for Refugee Students  
The Kompass UniBE project team advises and supports refugees interested in studying with their admission to a degree program at the University of Bern. With the Kompass UniBE project, it offers a university preparatory year.

About University Preparation (https://www.unibe.ch/universitaet/organisation/leitung_und_zentralbereich/vizerektorat_qualitaet_und_nachhaltige_entwicklung/kompass_unibe/index_ger.html)

Promoting an Active Culture of Engagement at UniBE and Beyond  
Engaged UniBE is an initiative of the University of Bern that aims to anchor the university within society. It helps to shape social developments together with stakeholders from Bern, the region, and the canton of Bern, as well as beyond.
With Engaged UniBE, knowledge transfer is promoted by supporting students, teachers, and staff in their engagement and exchange with society.

More about Engaged UniBE (https://engaged.unibe.ch/index_ger.html)

Title: Neue Fragebögen für die Lehrveranstaltungsevaluation und Evaluation der Leistungskontrollen
text:
Neue Fragebögen für die Lehrveranstaltungsevaluation und Evaluation der Leistungskontrollen
Basierend auf den Erfahrungen mit Evaluationen der letzten Jahre, wurden die Fragebögen für die Zwischen- und Schlussevaluation der Lehrveranstaltungen sowie die Evaluation der Leistungskontrollen (Prüfungen) in Zusammenarbeit mit den Fakultäten überarbeitet.  
Dieser Prozess der Überarbeitung ist nun abgeschlossen.

An der QSE-Kommission Sitzung vom 9. November 2022 wurden die überarbeiteten Versionen einstimmig angenommen. Sie kommen ab dem Frühjahrssemester 23 in Einsatz und werden die aktuellen Umfrageinstrumente ablösen.

Die neuen Umfrageinstrumente sind verständlicher formuliert, verzichten mehrheitlich auf den Hochschuldidaktik-Jargon, beinhalten mehr offene Fragen und sind generell kürzer als die bisherigen. Die Fragen sind breiter formuliert, so dass sie sich für die Evaluation vieler Lehrveranstaltungsformate eignen. Die Fragebögen berücksichtigen auch das Modell der Lehrqualität.

Ablauf der Evaluation einer  mündlichen Leistungskontrolle 

Anmeldung
Variante "Obligatorische ELK gemäss Evaluationsplan" • Ihre Leistungskontrolle wird durch die fakultäre QSE im KSL zur Evaluation angemeldet.  Variante "Freiwillige ELK" • Interessierte Dozierende melden ihre Leistungskontrolle bis spätestens Ende 10. Semesterwoche im KSL an (unter "Details" der Lehrveranstaltung, Menü "Dozierende").  Hinweis: Leistungskontrollen mit mehreren Terminen werden am 1. Termin evaluiert. Hinweis: Vorgezogene LKs müssen mind. 1 Woche vor dem ersten Prüfungstermin angemeldet werden. 

Erstellung Umfrage
Die Fachstelle LVE bereitet ab der 11. Semesterwoche die Onlineumfragen für die angemeldeten ELKs vor.  Jede Umfrage wird zeitlich so eingerichtet, dass sie im Anschluss an die Leistungskontrolle, also nach dem letzten geprüften Studierenden, durchgeführt werden muss. 

Information
Der/die Dozierende wird vor der Leistungskontrolle per Email von der Fachstelle LVE über die bevorstehende Evaluation und über das Schliessungsdatum der Umfrage informiert. 

Datenerhebung
Die Studierenden erhalten im Anschluss an die Prüfung (nach dem letzten geprüften Studierenden) eine Email mit dem Zugangslink zum Fragebogen.  • Die Umfrage bleibt 24h geöffnet und wird automatisch geschlossen. 

Bekanntgabe  der Noten 
Nach Schliessung der Umfrage (frühestens 24h nach Ende der Leistungskontrolle) kann der/die Dozierende bzw. eine verantwortliche Person die Noten im KSL eintragen und zur Freigabe ans Dekanat weiterleiten. Anschliessend bestätigen Sie der Fachstelle LVE (mailto:lehrevaluation@unibe.ch), dass Sie die Noten eingetragen und ans Dekanat weitergeleitet haben. Hinweis: Noten können bereits früher festgelegt, aber nicht den Studierenden bekanntgegeben werden. 

Prüfung Rücklaufquote 
Die Fachstelle LVE prüft die Freigabe der Noten und die Höhe der Rücklaufquote, um die Anonymität der Studierenden zu bewahren (Validität).

Title: MerkblattAblaufELKschriftlicheLKV4
text:
Ablauf der Evaluation einer  schriftlichen Leistungskontrolle 

Anmeldung 
Variante "Obligatorische ELK gemäss Evaluationsplan" • Ihre Leistungskontrolle wird durch die fakultäre QSE im KSL zur Evaluation angemeldet.  
Variante "Freiwillige ELK" • Interessierte Dozierende melden ihre Leistungskontrolle bis spätestens Ende 10. Semesterwoche im KSL an (unter "Details" der Lehrveranstaltung, Menü "Dozierende").  
Hinweis: Leistungskontrollen mit mehreren Prüfungsterminen werden am 1. Termin evaluiert. Hinweis: Vorgezogene LKs müssen mind. 1 Woche vor dem ersten Prüfungstermin angemeldet werden. 

Erstellung Umfrage 
• Die Fachstelle LVE bereitet ab der 11. Semesterwoche die Onlineumfragen für die angemeldeten ELKs vor.  
• Jede Umfrage wird zeitlich so eingerichtet, dass sie direkt im Anschluss an die Leistungskontrolle durchgeführt werden muss.

Information 
• Der/die Dozierende wird vor der Leistungskontrolle per Email von der Fachstelle LVE über die bevorstehende Evaluation und über das Schliessungsdatum der Umfrage informiert.

Datenerhebung 
• Die Studierenden erhalten im Anschluss an die Leistungskontrolle eine Email mit dem Zugangslink zum Fragebogen.  • Die Umfrage bleibt 4 Tage geöffnet und wird automatisch geschlossen. 

Bekanntgabe  der Noten 
  • Nach Schliessung der Umfrage (frühestens 4 Tage nach Ende der Leistungskontrolle) kann der/die Dozierende bzw. eine verantwortliche Person die Noten im KSL eintragen und zur Freigabe ans Dekanat weiterleiten. Anschliessend bestätigen Sie der Fachstelle LVE, dass Sie die Noten eingetragen und ans Dekanat weitergeleitet haben. Hinweis: Noten können bereits früher festgelegt, aber nicht den Studierenden bekanntgegeben werden. 

Prüfung Rücklaufquote 
• Die Fachstelle LVE prüft die Freigabe der Noten und die Höhe der Rücklaufquote, um die Anonymität der Studierenden zu bewahren (Validität). 

Report / Information 
• Ist die Evaluation valide, löst die Fachstelle LVE manuell den Versand des Reports mit der automatischen Zusammenfassung der Umfrageergebnisse sowie den Kommentaren der Studierenden aus. 
• Ist die Rücklaufquote zu gering oder waren die Noten bei der Befragung bereits bekannt, informiert die Fachstelle LVE den/die Dozierende, dass die Evaluation nicht gültig ist. • Das Ausbleiben des Reports bzw. einer Information kann der Fachstelle LVE gemeldet werden.  

Teilen der Ergebnisse  
• Der/die Dozierende oder prüfungsverantwortliche Person kann den Studierenden das Evaluationsergebnis mitteilen. 
• Bspw. kann die Präsentationsfolie auf der letzten Seite des Reports auf ILIAS publiziert oder per Email an die Studierenden versandt werden.  

Anpassungen 
• Falls nötig nimmt der/die Dozierende oder die prüfungsverantwortliche Person Anpassungen am didaktischen Konzept der Lehrveranstaltung und/oder der Leistungskontrolle vor. 

Nachhalten
• Die fakultäre Prüfungskommission führt stichprobenartige Überprüfung einer im Voraus durch die Fakultät definierten Auswahl an Leistungskontrollen durch. Sie erarbeitet Empfehlungen zur Verbesserung der Leistungskontrollen und verfasst einen anonymisierten Bericht zuhanden der Fakultät.

Process of Evaluating a Written Assessment

Registration  
Option "Mandatory ELK according to the Evaluation Plan"  
• Your assessment will be registered for evaluation in KSL by the faculty QSE.  
Option "Voluntary ELK"  
• Interested instructors must register their assessment in KSL by the end of the 10th semester week at the latest (under "Details" of the course, menu "Dozierende").  
Note: Assessments with multiple exam dates will be evaluated on the first date.  
Note: Early assessments must be registered at least 1 week before the first exam date.

Creating the Survey  
• The LVE office prepares the online surveys for the registered ELKs starting from the 11th semester week.  
• Each survey is scheduled so that it must be conducted immediately after the assessment.

Information  
• The instructor will be informed by email from the LVE office before the assessment about the upcoming evaluation and the closing date of the survey.

Data Collection  
• After the assessment, students will receive an email with the access link to the questionnaire.  
• The survey remains open for 4 days and then closes automatically.

Announcement of Grades  
• After the survey is closed (at the earliest 4 days after the end of the assessment), the instructor or a responsible person can enter the grades in KSL and forward them to the dean's office for approval. Afterwards, you confirm to the LVE office that you have entered the grades and forwarded them to the dean's office.  
Note: Grades may be determined earlier, but may not be communicated to the students.

Review of Response Rate  
• The LVE office checks the release of grades and the response rate in order to maintain student anonymity (validity).

Report / Information  
• If the evaluation is valid, the LVE office manually initiates the dispatch of the report with the automatic summary of the survey results as well as the students' comments.  
• If the response rate is too low or the grades were already known at the time of the survey, the LVE office informs the instructor that the evaluation is not valid.  
• The absence of the report or information can be reported to the LVE office.

Sharing the Results  
• The instructor or the person responsible for the assessment can communicate the evaluation results to the students.  
• For example, the presentation slide on the last page of the report can be published on ILIAS or sent to students by email.

Adjustments  
• If necessary, the instructor or the person responsible for the assessment will make adjustments to the didactic concept of the course and/or the assessment.

Follow-up  
• The faculty examination committee conducts random checks of an in advance defined selection of assessments by the faculty. It develops recommendations for improving assessments and writes an anonymized report for the faculty.

Title: Aktualisierung Rahmenkonzept
text:
Aktualisierung Rahmenkonzept
Das aktualisierte Rahmenkonzept für die Durchführung und Verwendung von Lehrveranstaltungsevaluationen an der UniBE wurde am 30. Januar 2024 von der Universitätsleitung einstimmig genehmigt. Damit hat sich die Universitätsleitung für die Kontinuität der Qualitätssicherung und -entwicklung auf Ebene der Lehrveranstaltungen ausgesprochen.

Die Aktualisierung, die 2023 in Zusammenarbeit mit den Fakultäten erfolgte, betrifft u.a.:

Sprachliche und formale Anpassungen
Präzisierung der Zuständigkeiten und bestimmter Prozesse
Handhabung der Ergebnisse und Datenschutz
Präzisere Beschreibung der Regelkreise
 

Im Rahmenkonzept sind die Mindestanforderungen an die Lehrveranstaltungsevaluation an der UniBE definiert und die universitätsweiten Prozesse festgehalten. Das Rahmenkonzept bietet somit allen Mitarbeitenden, die mit QSE-Aufgaben betraut sind, einen soliden Rahmen für ihre tägliche Arbeit.

Update of the Framework Concept  
The updated framework concept for the implementation and use of course evaluations at UniBE was unanimously approved by the university management on January 30, 2024. With this, the university management has affirmed its commitment to the continuity of quality assurance and development at the level of individual courses.

The update, which took place in 2023 in collaboration with the faculties, includes, among other things:

- Linguistic and formal adjustments
- Clarification of responsibilities and certain processes
- Handling of results and data protection
- More precise description of control loops

The framework concept defines the minimum requirements for course evaluation at UniBE and records the university-wide processes. Thus, the framework concept offers all staff members entrusted with QSE tasks a solid basis for their daily work.
